text.en: Order a parcel from Delhi to Chennai and it may travel by road, rail, air or even sea. Transport and communication tie the nation together.

Goods and services move by land, water and air. Transport, communication and trade are the lifelines of the national economy.
Roadways are cheaper for short distances and reach even remote villages. India has one of the largest road networks in the world.
Roads are classified as Golden Quadrilateral Super Expressways, National Highways, State Highways, District roads and Other roads, including border roads.
Railways are the principal mode of transport for goods and passengers. Indian Railways is the largest public sector undertaking.
Pipelines carry crude oil, natural gas and even water. Waterways are the cheapest means for heavy goods, and National Waterway 1 runs on the Ganga from Prayagraj to Haldia.
Major ports include Kandla, Mumbai, Chennai, Visakhapatnam, Kolkata and Kochi. Air transport is the fastest but costliest.
Communication includes post, telegram, radio, television, and the internet. Mass media and telecom connect distant places.
International trade is the exchange of goods among countries. A country must balance exports and imports, and tourism is also a trade.

problem.en: A truck carries 10 tonnes at Rs 5 per tonne per km. What is the cost for 400 km?

prompt.en: Why are transport and communication called lifelines?

points.en: Roadways, railways, pipelines, waterways and airways are the modes.
Chennai, Mumbai and Kandla are among major ports.
Communication includes mass media and internet.
International trade and tourism add to the economy.
